text:
sasha: Heads up — started seeing a regression on seq=1024 workloads after the driver bump to 530 on a subset of our farm. Latency up ~20% and some NaN traces. Looks like the FP8 kernel is being picked where previously it wasn't. :warning:
kevin: Can you paste the device query + runtime kernel-pick log from one of the failing machines?
sasha: Here's the relevant bits from deviceQuery and runtime log from box gpu-12:
```
Device 0: sm 86, name: A100-SXM4-40GB
Driver Version: 530.41.2  CUDA: 12.1
cudaGetDeviceAttr: cudaDevAttrComputeCapabilityMajor=8 minor=6
runtime: hw_caps: { sm:86, tensor_cores:true, bf16:true, fp8:false }
```
runtime log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] kernel_picker: candidate fp8_fast_k score=12 estimated_latency=8.3
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] kernel_picker: candidate bf16_tc_k score=11 estimated_latency=9.1
[2026-03-17T09:12:03Z] kernel_picker: chosen fp8_fast_k (policy: latency)
[2026-03-17T09:12:04Z] execution: output contains NaN at token 41
```
maria: Hmm — runtime hw_caps says fp8:false but picker still chose fp8_fast_k. That smells like a mismatch between capability detection and kernel availability scoring. Did the autotune profiles change?
infra-bot: autotune-ci: profile deploy complete: autotune/profiles/2026-03-17/v3 -> production (rollout 10%).
kevin: My suspicion: the new profile tuning gave fp8_fast_k a high score for sm86 due to microbench numbers collected on machines that actually had an experimental cuBLASLt FP8 path enabled. On machines without the cuBLASLt extension we should either not consider fp8 or require a runtime probe microbench to validate correctness (not just speed).
sasha: We saw the microbench outputs in the autotune artifact; they only ran throughput/latency numbers, no NaN/quality checks. So a fast-but-broken path got promoted. Oof.
maria: Short-term mitigation: add a deploy-time quirk to prefer stability for seq>512 or when batch_size>1. Example policy patch:
```
policy.kernel_gating:
  - condition: seq_len > 512 and batch_size > 1
    prefer: stable_kernels
```
kevin: Longer-term fix: update cap-detect to check for actual fp8 execution support. Two ideas:
  1) call cudaGetDeviceAttribute for attributes we already query AND run a tiny deterministic fp8 microkernel to check for NaNs (fast, <20ms).
  2) require autotune profiles to include a correctness sanity check (compare fp8 vs bf16 outputs on a small prompt set).
sasha: Agreed. For immediate rollback can someone push a hotfix that disables fp8 kernels in the picker when driver version < 531 or when hw_caps.fp8 == false? I can open a canary.
kevin: I'll send a small runtime patch: if (hw_caps.fp8 == false) score(fp8_k) -= 1000; also add env var REDWOOD_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FP8=true for emergency. Pushing PR now.
perfbot: perf-scan: comparing profile v2 -> v3 across 20 hosts:
  seq=512 median latency: +3%
  seq=1024 median latency: +22% (p95 +40%)
  failures: 4 hosts showed NaN/invalid tokens with fp8_fast_k
perfbot: hosts affected: gpu-12, gpu-19, gpu-27, gpu-42
sasha: Thanks — can we canary the hotfix to the 4 affected hosts first? I want to validate no regressions for seq<=512.
maria: I'll coordinate canary. Also we should add an autotune gating job that runs a correctness diff for fp8 candidates before publishing profiles.
kevin: PR: runtime#4823 — adds fp8 sanity probe + env var + quick policy gating. Will request review from @maria and @sasha.
sasha: Nice. After merge let's re-run autotune on a small subset and re-evaluate. :thumbsup:
kevin: Also logging TODO: persist kernel_picker.choice_reason in trace so we can see why a kernel was chosen (perf score vs fallback).
sasha: Good call. That would've saved time here.
